input.question: What position does John Greny currently or formerly hold?

documents.text: In the heart of the Roman Catholic Church, a revered figure emerged to guide the faithful flock. John Greny, a devoted servant of the Lord, had been entrusted with the sacred responsibility of leading a diocese as its diocesan bishop. This esteemed position, one of great trust and authority, was not taken lightly, and Greny's appointment was a testament to his unwavering commitment to the Church. As the bishop in pastoral charge of his diocese, Greny's duties were multifaceted and far-reaching. He was responsible for the spiritual well-being of his congregation, providing guidance, support, and wisdom to those seeking solace in the teachings of Christ. His role was not limited to mere ceremonial duties, but rather, he was an active shepherd, tending to the needs of his flock with compassion, empathy, and understanding. One of the most compelling pieces of evidence supporting Greny's position as diocesan bishop was his involvement in the appointment of parish priests within his diocese. As the spiritual leader of his community, it was his duty to identify and ordain worthy candidates to serve as priests, ensuring the continued growth and vitality of the Church. This responsibility was not taken lightly, and Greny's careful consideration and discernment in this process demonstrated his deep understanding of the Church's teachings and his commitment to its mission. Furthermore, Greny's role in the governance of his diocese was another key indicator of his position as diocesan bishop. He was responsible for overseeing the administration of the diocese, making key decisions regarding the allocation of resources, and ensuring the financial stability of the Church. This level of authority and responsibility was a hallmark of a diocesan bishop, and Greny's leadership in this regard was a testament to his ability to navigate the complexities of Church governance. In addition, Greny's participation in regional and national ecclesiastical gatherings provided further evidence of his position as diocesan bishop. As a respected voice within the Church, he was often called upon to share his insights and expertise with fellow bishops and clergy, providing guidance on matters of doctrine, discipline, and pastoral care. His involvement in these gatherings demonstrated his recognition as a leader within the Church, and his contributions were highly valued by his peers. The sacramental life of the Church was another area where Greny's role as diocesan bishop was evident.
